obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (a) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective, or the effect of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or a group of persons by appreciably impairing their ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing them to take a decision that they would not have otherwise taken in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person, another person or group of persons significant harm.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person placing on the market, putting into service, or using an AI system (provider, deployer, or any other party)

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not deploy subliminal techniques beyond conscious perception
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness SHALL be prohibited where those techniques have the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or a group of persons by appreciably impairing their ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing them to take a decision that they would not otherwise have taken, in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person, another person or a group of persons significant harm.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT deploy subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness that materially distort behaviour and cause or are reasonably likely to cause significant harm
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not deploy purposefully manipulative techniques
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys purposefully manipulative techniques SHALL be prohibited where those techniques have the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or a group of persons by appreciably impairing their ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing them to take a decision that they would not otherwise have taken, in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person, another person or a group of persons significant harm.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT deploy purposefully manipulative techniques that appreciably impair informed decision-making and cause or are reasonably likely to cause significant harm
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not deploy purposefully deceptive techniques
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys purposefully deceptive techniques SHALL be prohibited where those techniques have the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or a group of persons by appreciably impairing their ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing them to take a decision that they would not otherwise have taken, in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person, another person or a group of persons significant harm.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT deploy purposefully deceptive techniques that appreciably impair informed decision-making and cause or are reasonably likely to cause significant harm
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: The prohibition is triggered by significant harm or reasonable likelihood thereof
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition applies when the manipulative/subliminal/deceptive technique causes or is REASONABLY LIKELY to cause significant harm — actual harm is not required, likelihood suffices

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (b) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person or another person significant harm.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person placing on the market, putting into service, or using an AI system

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not exploit age-related vulnerabilities
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to their age SHALL be prohibited where the exploitation has the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person or another person significant harm.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT exploit vulnerabilities due to age (e.g., targeting children or elderly) to materially distort behaviour causing significant harm
_history.description: AI systems must not exploit age-related vulnerabilities (children, elderly)
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not exploit disability-related vulnerabilities
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to their disability SHALL be prohibited where the exploitation has the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person or another person significant harm.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT exploit vulnerabilities due to disability (cognitive, physical, sensory) to materially distort behaviour causing significant harm
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not exploit social or economic vulnerability
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to a specific social or economic situation SHALL be prohibited where the exploitation has the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person or another person significant harm.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT exploit vulnerabilities due to specific social or economic situation (poverty, homelessness, immigration status) to materially distort behaviour causing significant harm
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: Both a distortion element (objective or effect) and a harm element (actual or reasonably likely) must be present
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition is triggered when exploitation is carried out with the objective OR the effect of materially distorting behaviour (actual distortion is not required where it is the objective) AND causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm (actual harm is not required where it is reasonably likely)

_history.requirement: The prohibition is triggered when exploitation BOTH materially distorts behaviour AND causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm — both elements are required
_history.description: Both material distortion of behaviour and significant harm must be present
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (ba) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable natural person’s intimate parts, or of an identifiable natural person engaged in sexually explicit activities, without that person’s freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation or manipulation.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person placing on the market, putting into service or using such an AI system. Art. 5(1a)(a) limits the placing-on-the-market / putting-into-service limb to intended-purpose or foreseeable-outcome-without-adequate-safeguards cases; Art. 5(1a)(b) limits the use limb to a deployer using the system for that purpose.

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not generate or manipulate realistic intimate or sexually explicit material of identifiable persons without their consent
decomposed_atoms.requirement: An AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable natural person's intimate parts, or of an identifiable natural person engaged in sexually explicit activities, SHALL NOT be placed on the market, put into service or used unless that person gave consent meeting the standard in ncii_consent_standard

decomposed_atoms.description: Only consent with all five statutory qualities lifts the prohibition (Art. 5(1)(ba))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition is lifted only by the depicted person's consent that is freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous AND explicit, given for that particular generation or manipulation — all five qualities are required

decomposed_atoms.description: Placing on the market / putting into service is prohibited where NCII generation is the intended purpose (Art. 5(1a)(a)(i))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Placing on the market or putting into service is prohibited where generating or manipulating such material is the intended purpose of the AI system

decomposed_atoms.description: Placing on the market / putting into service is also prohibited where NCII is a foreseeable, reproducible outcome (Art. 5(1a)(a)(ii))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Placing on the market or putting into service is also prohibited where the system's design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make such generation or manipulation a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without requiring significant technical modification, and the safeguards condition in ncii_market_trigger_inadequate_safeguards is met

decomposed_atoms.description: Foreseeable-outcome route applies unless BOTH prevention and misuse-correction safeguards exist (Art. 5(1a)(a)(ii))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Under the foreseeable-outcome route, the system escapes the prohibition only if it has BOTH (1) reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards that reliably prevent such generation or manipulation, taking into account reasonably foreseeable misuse, AND (2) reasonable and adequate measures to correct observed or reported misuse — lacking either one means the prohibition applies

decomposed_atoms.description: Use is prohibited where the deployer uses the system to generate or manipulate such material (Art. 5(1a)(b))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Use of the AI system is prohibited where the deployer uses it for the purpose of generating or manipulating such material

decomposed_atoms.description: Manipulation that does not increase exposure or alter sexual activity is not manipulation (Art. 5(1b))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Manipulation that neither increases the exposure of any depicted intimate parts nor alters the nature of any depicted sexually explicit activities does not constitute manipulation for point (ba)

exceptions.description: Not prohibited where the identifiable person gave freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation or manipulation
exceptions.note: Art. 5(1)(ba) does not specify which actor must collect, verify or document the consent. Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12: for AI systems intended to generate or manipulate such material, the measures and other safeguards should include appropriate means for the distribution of the AI system aimed at enabling the reliable collection and demonstration of the depicted person's consent, in compliance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

cross_references.context: Art. 5(1a) conditions points (ba) and (bb) (intended purpose / foreseeable outcome without adequate safeguards / deployer purpose); Art. 5(1b) applies to point (ba) only
Art. 113, third paragraph, point (a), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: points (ba) and (bb) and Art. 5(1a) and (1b) apply from 2 December 2026

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (bb) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates material or performance within the meaning of Article 2, points (c) and (e), of Directive 2011/93/EU, except where a ‘without right’ defence applies under national law.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person placing on the market, putting into service or using such an AI system. Art. 5(1a)(a) limits the placing-on-the-market / putting-into-service limb to intended-purpose or foreseeable-outcome-without-adequate-safeguards cases; Art. 5(1a)(b) limits the use limb to a deployer using the system for that purpose.

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not generate or manipulate child sexual abuse material or performance (Directive 2011/93/EU Art. 2(c), (e))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: An AI system that generates or manipulates material or performance within the meaning of Article 2, points (c) and (e), of Directive 2011/93/EU SHALL NOT be placed on the market, put into service or used

decomposed_atoms.description: National-law 'without right' defence (Art. 5(1)(bb))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition does not apply where a 'without right' defence applies under national law

decomposed_atoms.description: Placing on the market / putting into service is prohibited where such generation is the intended purpose (Art. 5(1a)(a)(i))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Placing on the market or putting into service is prohibited where generating or manipulating such material or performance is the intended purpose of the AI system

decomposed_atoms.description: Placing on the market / putting into service is also prohibited where such output is a foreseeable, reproducible outcome (Art. 5(1a)(a)(ii))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Placing on the market or putting into service is also prohibited where the system's design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make such generation or manipulation a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without requiring significant technical modification, and the safeguards condition in csam_market_trigger_inadequate_safeguards is met

decomposed_atoms.description: Foreseeable-outcome route applies unless BOTH prevention and misuse-correction safeguards exist (Art. 5(1a)(a)(ii))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Under the foreseeable-outcome route, the system escapes the prohibition only if it has BOTH (1) reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards that reliably prevent such generation or manipulation, taking into account reasonably foreseeable misuse, AND (2) reasonable and adequate measures to correct observed or reported misuse — lacking either one means the prohibition applies

decomposed_atoms.description: Use is prohibited where the deployer uses the system to generate or manipulate such material (Art. 5(1a)(b))
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Use of the AI system is prohibited where the deployer uses it for the purpose of generating or manipulating such material or performance

exceptions.description: Not prohibited where a 'without right' defence applies under national law
exceptions.note: Depends on the national law of the Member State concerned. Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 13: this includes activities carried out under domestic legal powers, such as the legitimate generation or manipulation of such material by the authorities in order to conduct criminal proceedings or to prevent, detect or investigate crime, and the legitimate use of the AI system for red-teaming and evaluation activities to assess its compliance with the prohibition.

cross_references.context: Defines the material and performance covered by Art. 5(1)(bb). The Directive text is not in ComplianceLint's source set; cited, not paraphrased
Art. 5(1a) conditions point (bb) (intended purpose / foreseeable outcome without adequate safeguards / deployer purpose)
Art. 113, third paragraph, point (a), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: points (ba) and (bb) and Art. 5(1a) and (1b) apply from 2 December 2026

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (c) the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups of persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics, with the social score leading to either or both of the following: (i) detrimental or unfavourable treatment of certain natural persons or groups of persons in social contexts that are unrelated to the contexts in which the data was originally generated or collected; (ii) detrimental or unfavourable treatment of certain natural persons or groups of persons that is unjustified or disproportionate to their social behaviour or its gravity.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person — the final text removed the earlier draft limitation to public authorities; social scoring by private entities is also prohibited

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not produce social scores leading to detrimental treatment in unrelated contexts
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups of persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics SHALL be prohibited where the resulting social score leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment of certain natural persons or groups of persons in social contexts unrelated to the contexts in which the data was originally generated or collected.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT evaluate or classify persons based on social behaviour or personal characteristics where the resulting score leads to detrimental treatment in social contexts UNRELATED to where the data was originally generated
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not produce social scores leading to disproportionate treatment
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups of persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics SHALL be prohibited where the resulting social score leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment of certain natural persons or groups of persons that is unjustified or disproportionate to their social behaviour or its gravity.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT evaluate or classify persons based on social behaviour or personal characteristics where the resulting score leads to detrimental treatment that is UNJUSTIFIED or DISPROPORTIONATE to the behaviour or its gravity
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: The prohibition covers scores based on known, inferred, or predicted characteristics
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition applies whether the social score is based on KNOWN, INFERRED, or PREDICTED personal or personality characteristics — all three bases are covered

decomposed_atoms.description: The prohibition covers scoring over a period of time
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition applies to evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups of persons over a certain period of time; the text does not further define the length of that period

_history.requirement: The prohibition applies to evaluation or classification over a certain period of time — aggregate behavioural scoring, not single-instance assessments in isolation
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (d) the placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of an AI system for making risk assessments of natural persons in order to assess or predict the risk of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics; this prohibition shall not apply to AI systems used to support the human assessment of the involvement of a person in a criminal activity, which is already based on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies broadly, but primarily relevant to law enforcement and justice system actors

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not assess criminal risk based solely on profiling
decomposed_atoms.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT assess or predict the risk of a person committing a criminal offence based SOLELY on profiling of that person

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not assess criminal risk based solely on personality traits
decomposed_atoms.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT assess or predict criminal risk based solely on assessing a person's personality traits and characteristics — without objective factual basis

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception: AI may support human assessment when based on objective verifiable facts
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition does NOT apply when AI is used to SUPPORT (not replace) human assessment of involvement in criminal activity that is ALREADY based on objective, verifiable facts DIRECTLY linked to criminal activity

decomposed_atoms.description: The exception has three cumulative conditions
decomposed_atoms.requirement: For the exception to apply, ALL three conditions must be met: (1) the AI supports (not replaces) human assessment; (2) the assessment is based on objective, verifiable facts; (3) those facts are directly linked to criminal activity

cross_references.context: AI systems supporting criminal justice that are not prohibited under Art. 5(1)(d) may still be classified as high-risk under Art. 6

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (e) the placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person — no exceptions exist for this prohibition

decomposed_atoms.description: Must not create facial recognition databases by scraping the internet
decomposed_atoms.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT create or expand facial recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet

decomposed_atoms.description: Must not create facial recognition databases by scraping CCTV footage
decomposed_atoms.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT create or expand facial recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from CCTV footage

decomposed_atoms.description: The prohibition targets untargeted scraping specifically
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition applies to UNTARGETED scraping — bulk, indiscriminate collection. Targeted collection with lawful basis is not covered by this specific prohibition

decomposed_atoms.description: Both creating new databases and expanding existing ones are prohibited
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition covers both CREATING new facial recognition databases AND EXPANDING existing ones through untargeted scraping

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (f) the placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person deploying emotion recognition in workplace or education settings

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not infer emotions in the workplace
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the area of workplace SHALL be prohibited, except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons. For purposes of determining whether a system constitutes emotion recognition, Art. 3(39) requires an AI system for the purpose of identifying or inferring emotions or intentions of natural persons on the basis of their biometric data; labels such as "attention" or "engagement" do not by themselves determine whether Art. 5(1)(f) applies.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT be used to infer emotions of persons in the area of workplace — including employee mood detection, engagement monitoring, hiring interview emotion analysis
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: AI systems must not infer emotions in educational institutions
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the area of education institutions SHALL be prohibited, except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons. For purposes of determining whether a system constitutes emotion recognition, Art. 3(39) requires an AI system for the purpose of identifying or inferring emotions or intentions of natural persons on the basis of their biometric data; labels such as "attention" or "engagement" do not by themselves determine whether Art. 5(1)(f) applies.

_history.requirement: An AI system SHALL NOT be used to infer emotions of persons in the area of education institutions — including student attention monitoring, engagement tracking, and emotional state assessment
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception for medical purposes
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition does NOT apply where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical reasons (Art. 5(1)(f)); Recital 44 gives systems intended for therapeutical use as an example. Art. 5(1)(f) states no separate documentation condition.

_history.requirement: The prohibition does NOT apply when the AI system is intended for medical reasons — e.g., therapeutic monitoring, clinical assessment, mental health support. The medical purpose must be genuine and documented
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception for safety purposes
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition does NOT apply where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for safety reasons. Detecting physical states such as fatigue or pain (e.g., fatigue detection for professional pilots or drivers) is not emotion recognition at all (Recital 18) and therefore falls outside the prohibition rather than within this exception

_history.requirement: The prohibition does NOT apply when the AI system is intended for safety reasons — e.g., driver drowsiness detection, operator fatigue monitoring in safety-critical operations. The safety purpose must be genuine and documented
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (g) the placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation; this prohibition does not cover any labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets, such as images, based on biometric data or categorizing of biometric data in the area of law enforcement.
obligations.addressee_note: Applies to any natural or legal person, with narrow exceptions for dataset labelling and law enforcement

decomposed_atoms.description: Must not use biometric data to infer race
decomposed_atoms.requirement: A biometric categorization system SHALL NOT categorize persons based on biometric data to deduce or infer their race

decomposed_atoms.description: Must not use biometric data to infer political opinions
decomposed_atoms.requirement: A biometric categorization system SHALL NOT categorize persons based on biometric data to deduce or infer their political opinions

decomposed_atoms.description: Must not use biometric data to infer trade union membership
decomposed_atoms.requirement: A biometric categorization system SHALL NOT categorize persons based on biometric data to deduce or infer their trade union membership

decomposed_atoms.description: Must not use biometric data to infer religious or philosophical beliefs
decomposed_atoms.requirement: A biometric categorization system SHALL NOT categorize persons based on biometric data to deduce or infer their religious or philosophical beliefs

decomposed_atoms.description: Must not use biometric data to infer sex life or sexual orientation
decomposed_atoms.requirement: A biometric categorization system SHALL NOT categorize persons based on biometric data to deduce or infer their sex life or sexual orientation

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception for lawful labelling/filtering of biometric datasets
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition does NOT apply to labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets — e.g., annotating training data images based on biometric data, provided acquisition was lawful

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception for law enforcement biometric categorization
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition does NOT apply to categorizing of biometric data in the area of law enforcement — subject to applicable legal basis and safeguards

obligations.source_quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited: (h) the use of 'real-time' remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement, unless and in so far as such use is strictly necessary for one of the following objectives: (i) the targeted search for specific victims of abduction, trafficking in human beings or sexual exploitation of human beings, as well as the search for missing persons; (ii) the prevention of a specific, substantial and imminent threat to the life or physical safety of natural persons or a genuine and present or genuine and foreseeable threat of a terrorist attack; (iii) the localisation or identification of a person suspected of having committed a criminal offence, for the purpose of conducting a criminal investigation or prosecution or executing a criminal penalty for offences referred to in Annex II and punishable in the Member State concerned by a custodial sentence or a detention order for a maximum period of at least four years.
obligations.addressee_note: This prohibition specifically targets law enforcement use in publicly accessible spaces. Non-law-enforcement real-time biometric ID in public spaces is regulated under Art. 6 as high-risk

decomposed_atoms.description: Real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces is prohibited for law enforcement
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The use of real-time remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces SHALL be prohibited for law enforcement purposes — this is the default rule

decomposed_atoms.description: Real-time means live or near-live processing without significant delay
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition covers 'real-time' remote biometric identification: the capturing of biometric data, comparison and identification all occur without a significant delay, comprising instant identification and limited short delays in order to avoid circumvention (Art. 3(42)). Post-remote biometric identification is not prohibited by Art. 5(1)(h) merely by being post-remote; remote biometric identification systems, including post-remote systems, are listed as high-risk under Art. 6(2) and Annex III, point 1(a), in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law.

_history.requirement: The prohibition covers 'real-time' systems — live biometric matching, not post-facto analysis. Post-facto analysis is regulated as high-risk under Art. 6 but not banned
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: The prohibition applies only in publicly accessible spaces, whether publicly or privately owned
decomposed_atoms.requirement: The prohibition applies in PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE spaces: any publicly or privately owned physical place accessible to an undetermined number of natural persons, regardless of whether certain conditions for access may apply and regardless of the potential capacity restrictions (Art. 3(44)).

_history.requirement: The prohibition applies in PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE spaces — streets, parks, transport hubs, shopping centres. Private or access-controlled spaces are not covered by this specific prohibition
_history.description: The prohibition applies only in publicly accessible spaces
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception (i): targeted search for victims or missing persons
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Exception: real-time biometric ID MAY be used for targeted search for specific victims of abduction, trafficking, sexual exploitation, or search for missing persons — strictly necessary use only

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception (ii): prevention of imminent threats or terrorist attacks
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Exception: real-time biometric ID MAY be used for prevention of a specific, substantial, and imminent threat to life or physical safety, or a genuine and present/foreseeable terrorist threat — strictly necessary use only

decomposed_atoms.description: Exception (iii): identification of suspects for serious crimes
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Exception: real-time biometric ID MAY be used for localization or identification of suspects of criminal offences punishable by custodial sentence of at least 4 years, for offences listed in Annex II — strictly necessary use only

decomposed_atoms.description: All exceptions require prior authorisation by a judicial authority or a binding independent administrative authority
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Use under any exception SHALL require prior authorisation granted by a judicial authority or an independent administrative authority whose decision is binding (Art. 5(3)) — except in a duly justified situation of urgency, where authorisation must be requested without undue delay, at the latest within 24 hours. If authorisation is rejected, use must stop with immediate effect and all data, results and outputs must be immediately discarded and deleted

_history.requirement: Use under any exception SHALL require prior judicial authorization — except in duly justified urgency, where authorization must be sought within 24 hours. If authorization is refused, use must cease immediately and all data deleted
_history.description: All exceptions require prior judicial authorization
_history.reason: consensus-lock 2026-10-02 §6 (o3 sweep + Claude verification against Art 5 / Art 3 / Recital 18)

decomposed_atoms.description: All exceptions must comply with proportionality and necessity requirements
decomposed_atoms.requirement: Use under any exception SHALL only serve to confirm the identity of the specifically targeted individual (Art. 5(2)) and shall take into account (a) the nature of the situation giving rise to the possible use, in particular the seriousness, probability and scale of the harm that would be caused if the system were not used, and (b) the consequences of the use for the rights and freedoms of all persons concerned, in particular the seriousness, probability and scale of those consequences. The use SHALL comply with necessary and proportionate safeguards and conditions in accordance with the national law authorising the use, in particular temporal, geographic and personal limitations. It may be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment under Art. 27 and registered the system in the EU database under Art. 49; in duly justified cases of urgency, use may commence before registration provided registration is completed without undue delay. Each use SHALL be notified to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority pursuant to Art. 5(4).

_history.requirement: Use under any exception SHALL be subject to temporal, geographic, and personal limitations, fundamental rights impact assessment, notification to market surveillance authority, and registration in the EU database (Art. 49)

scope_notes.absolute_prohibitions_no_exceptions: ART05-PRO-1a, ART05-PRO-1b, ART05-PRO-1c, ART05-PRO-1e — prohibitions with no exceptions (the significant-harm threshold still applies to ART05-PRO-1a and ART05-PRO-1b)
scope_notes.prohibitions_with_narrow_exceptions: ART05-PRO-1d (support of a human assessment of involvement in criminal activity that is already based on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity), ART05-PRO-1f (medical or safety reasons), ART05-PRO-1g (labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets; categorising biometric data in the area of law enforcement), ART05-PRO-1h (three law-enforcement objectives, subject to Art. 5(2)-(5), including prior authorisation under Art. 5(3) except that in a duly justified situation of urgency use may commence before authorisation if authorisation is requested without undue delay and at the latest within 24 hours), ART05-PRO-1ba (the depicted person's freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent), ART05-PRO-1bb ('without right' defence under national law)
scope_notes.enforcement_date: 2025-02-02 — Art. 5 applies from this date (Art. 113, third paragraph, point (a)); points (ba) and (bb) and paragraphs (1a) and (1b), added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, apply from 2026-12-02
scope_notes.penalty_tier: Highest under the AI Act: up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
scope_notes.omnibus_2026_additions: ART05-PRO-1ba (non-consensual intimate material) and ART05-PRO-1bb (child sexual abuse material) added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; applicable from 2026-12-02; conditioned by Art. 5(1a) and (for 1ba) Art. 5(1b)
